---
title: "Custom Apps"
sidebarTitle: "Overview"
description: "Operating software built on the World Model, hosted by Oxygen"
---

**Custom Apps** are the applications a team runs its operations on, such as a
store checklist, a staffing planner, or a pricing console, built on Oxygen and
hosted by it. Each app reads the same [World Model](/guide/build/world-model)
as every agent and dashboard, and can write the data its users produce back
into the platform. An app has three parts:

- A **React interface**, built with the Oxygen SDK, that queries metrics, runs
  agents, and embeds chat with a few hooks and drop-in components.
- **Oxygen Functions**, server-side TypeScript that ships with the app for
  work the browser shouldn't do, triggered by users, schedules, or verified
  webhooks.
- **Its own data**: facts appended to [Airhouse](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airhouse),
  editable records in Postgres, and files in app storage.

## Why it matters

- **Built on the World Model.** Apps inherit the business model rather than
  rebuilding it: the same metric definitions, the drivers behind each metric,
  and the agents that explain them. The World Model interface for apps is in
  preview.
- **Real applications, not just dashboards.** Apps record what happens in the
  business, from completed checklists to bookings and uploaded files, and that
  data becomes part of what the World Model can measure.
- **Secure by default.** There is no API key in an app: access rides on the
  viewer's Oxygen session and is scoped to project membership, each function
  can do only what it declares, and every webhook is verified before it runs.
- **One step to ship.** Interface and functions are versioned and published
  together, and appear to the team on the Oxygen home page.

## Where it fits

Custom apps are the top layer of Oxygen. [Data Infrastructure](/guide/build/data-infrastructure)
gets data in, the [World Model](/guide/build/world-model) defines what it
means, and apps and [agents](/guide/build/agents) put it to work. Because apps
write their facts into Airhouse, the work done in an app feeds the same
metrics that measure it.
